section_summary: This section closes a State Department letter about remedies for Allied patent owners in Japan, then addresses Northern Equipment Company's yen balance and India's approval of a proposal on Japanese patents outside Japan. A despatch from Belgrade reports Yugoslavia's position on patent information and Japanese rights, followed by a brief file note about a delayed interim reply.

people.role: Officer in Charge, Economic Affairs, Office of Northeast Asian Affairs

subfiles.title: Letter on Allied patent remedies and claims against Japan
subfiles.from: Edward W. Doherty, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains available patent remedies and directs the recipient to the Civil Property Custodian.
subfiles.summary: The Department declines to process the debt as a war claim and points to remedies under Far Eastern Commission patent policy.

subfiles.title: Northern Equipment Company inquiry about yen deposit
subfiles.about: The company asks whether its yen balance can be transferred in dollars.
subfiles.summary: Northern Equipment asks about converting and transferring ¥71,278 held in its Special Property Administration Account.

subfiles.title: Reply on withdrawal and conversion of yen deposit
subfiles.from: Hawley L. Smith, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.to: E. W. Scarlett, Northern Equipment Company
subfiles.about: The Department explains conditions for withdrawing funds and restrictions on converting or exporting them.
subfiles.summary: An agent in Japan may withdraw available funds subject to a claim settlement agreement; current rules prohibit dollar conversion and transfer abroad.

subfiles.title: India's approval of proposal on Japanese patents outside Japan
subfiles.about: India approves a draft proposal and asks what action follows.
subfiles.summary: Vaidyanathan reports India's approval of the October 5 proposal on Japanese patents outside Japan.

subfiles.title: Reply to India on Japanese patents proposal
subfiles.about: The Department says further action depends on outstanding replies.
subfiles.summary: Dixon acknowledges India's approval and promises guidance once all replies arrive.

subfiles.title: Information from Yugoslav Ministry of Foreign Affairs for Japanese Board of Patents
subfiles.from: William A. Fowler, American Embassy, Belgrade
subfiles.about: The Embassy relays Yugoslavia's response to Japanese patent inquiries.
subfiles.summary: The Yugoslav ministry points to Propriété Industrielle for its patent laws and says recognition of Japanese rights is tied to a peace treaty with Japan.

subfiles.title: File note on delayed interim reply
subfiles.about: The writer records receiving a letter from Miss Hadley and apologizes for a delayed interim reply.
subfiles.summary: Notes transfer of a letter and delay in its attached interim reply.
